cases.rationale: Rejects rewriting provenance, registers and scopes the new source, preserves the old claim and UDR, and requires a scope/method comparison before any supersession. It separates global guidance from project-local overrides and calls for downstream impact review. The completion state remains open, identifies the owner and next decision, and explicitly says behavioral effectiveness is unverified because no eval was run.

cases.rationale: Correctly rejects implementation readiness and post-hoc tests as a substitute for prior agreement. It distinguishes rules, examples, implementation, and test evidence; keeps policy questions open; proposes executable layers and stable traceability; and avoids assuming transport architecture. The example coverage is strong but leaves some requested concrete boundary cases for a future session, so decision correctness loses one point. It clearly marks the map and tests as planned, not executed.

Rejects a hard-coded family exception, reopens the expected rule and examples, treats overrides as evidence rather than proof of a code defect, and proposes investigating operator decisions, Finance policy, and Legacy data.
